## US Escalates Pressure on Venezuela with Sanctions and Threats of Military Action

In a tense week for US-Venezuela relations, the United States government intensified its pressure campaign against the government of Nicolás Maduro, imposing new sanctions and threatening ground operations. The actions, occurring between December 6 and December 13, 2025, marked a significant escalation in the ongoing standoff between the two nations.

The week's events began with the United States seizing a large crude carrier, the Skipper, on December 10, the first such vessel seizure related to Venezuela. [aljazeera.com](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEkgLtLry6osM08nj2rVUVI2THbwnrxfO5cED8rgkvynkG-m0sEfstym7eqvUV9dKsb1aLo0SlEu6UpwTt2--vhbDG2z7kgIgG1u5SPLaN1Od2oh0w64cpqJrJB91Pp38AGn0007go_Go3aRCGDMoYJtLQwKrpLYE1U11aD4zrwtEOZUJw6WlBgQvfqjeVjPpgmqmMzyyQ8BRwqNfABIciJCorZ) This was followed by the Treasury Department announcing new sanctions on December 11, targeting individuals described as "corrupt nephews and backers" of President Maduro. [state.gov](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGxVXVJ9USY1VogycRMau1CGYrmUPwyrQKp8Lan3lM1iKOohGK88Zqyf7-60inmHsyHJTLYDx6LStzqsdVjOA_ro4woMtpREr8zSNObB9ru6H6ZHyPZAwBB9bppN8clj5dwN1WScpddNGyXT1__fcji_g==) [treasury.gov](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHXhZur7Nlqsc1_ke5gCpQ4eg0mvglLVKSxa0xYuBCdhr6YsgHiUPblNwObyN1XlnRHBJozPXrh-3_YfOj15XENNyPr8eYb1HXA6df_K7XMDQ9wmKCArFu8rG2FfNwC0nhDTp1qlkapi1NbtZ5QsOcbEgkvO__WsVqn5kyAWb7YP4Q2lXpTscDnOXRAFBnPVUwSkU4W9-gdLTly) These designations were part of a broader set of actions related to counter-narcotics and non-proliferation. [treasury.gov](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHXhZur7Nlqsc1_ke5gCpQ4eg0mvglLVKSxa0xYuBCdhr6YsgHiUPblNwObyN1XlnRHBJozPXrh-3_YfOj15XENNyPr8eYb1HXA6df_K7XMDQ9wmKCArFu8rG2FfNwC0nhDTp1qlkapi1NbtZ5QsOcbEgkvO__WsVqn5kyAWb7YP4Q2lXpTscDnOXRAFBnPVUwSkU4W9-gdLTly)

The seizure of the oil tanker drew a swift condemnation from Venezuelan Defense Minister Vladimir Padrino Lopez on December 12. [youtube.com](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQG2Ed-66YFPzCcl5Cje7g3En6UhZ9aA70rrg28U8llhWFVyvJ-F2iLlYVMvag5U-fFeqAYWEU_tTZcWY1x8wbPGWBe7PVeCf4E4iZdyd7r_sw_fEswqDF12xvOHFTl1Qbfvla9iIA==)

The situation escalated further on December 13, when US President Donald Trump stated that land strikes on Venezuela could be coming "soon." [youtube.com](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQG2Ed-66YFPzCcl5Cje7g3En6UhZ9aA70rrg28U8llhWFVyvJ-F2iLlYVMvag5U-fFeqAYWEU_tTZcWY1x8wbPGWBe7PVeCf4E4iZdyd7r_sw_fEswqDF12xvOHFTl1Qbfvla9iIA==) President Trump asserted that his administration's actions had led to a 92% decrease in drug trafficking by sea from Venezuela. grounding_supports.segment_text: The week's events began with the United States seizing a large crude carrier, the Skipper, on December 10, the first such vessel seizure related to Venezuela.
This was followed by the Treasury Department announcing new sanctions on December 11, targeting individuals described as "corrupt nephews and backers" of President Maduro.
These designations were part of a broader set of actions related to counter-narcotics and non-proliferation.
The seizure of the oil tanker drew a swift condemnation from Venezuelan Defense Minister Vladimir Padrino Lopez on December 12.
The situation escalated further on December 13, when US President Donald Trump stated that land strikes on Venezuela could be coming "soon."
President Trump asserted that his administration's actions had led to a 92% decrease in drug trafficking by sea from Venezuela.
These threats of military intervention coincided with the imposition of fresh sanctions targeting ships and shipping companies involved in Venezuela's oil sector.
An article published on December 12 hinted at the significance of these developments, titled "What Trump's latest dramatic Venezuela move means."

Reports from later in December indicated the US had begun a maritime blockade, intercepting tankers carrying Venezuelan crude, and had ordered a "total and complete blockade" of sanctioned oil tankers.
The US justified its increased military presence in the Southern Caribbean as part of a "non-international armed conflict" against drug cartels.
By the end of the month, the US Department of the Treasury was targeting oil traders engaged in sanctions evasion for the Maduro regime.
